transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I've been experiencing continuous weight loss recently because I've only been eating very small amounts of food. That's really the main reason I'm visiting the clinic today.
Do you restrict your food intake because you're afraid of gaining weight or becoming overweight?

Yes, I strictly limit what I eat because I have an overwhelming fear of gaining weight or becoming fat. Even the thought of putting on any weight is terrifying to me, so I only allow myself to eat very small portions.
Can you tell me your current weight and height, or do you know your body mass index?
I don't really know what my exact height and weight are right now, and I'm not sure of my BMI either. To be honest, I prefer not to look at the scale because seeing the numbers makes me too anxious.
Do you think you are underweight or at a normal weight, despite what others might say or what the scale might show?

I definitely don't think I'm underweight; if anything, my weight feels completely normal. Other people keep worrying and telling me I'm too thin, but when I look in the mirror, I still see areas that I need to tone up and lose weight from. Their concerns just seem really unnecessary to me.
Do you ever experience any rituals or compulsions related to food or eating, such as excessive exercise or purging, as a way to cope with your fear of gaining weight?
No, I don't engage in purging or excessive exercise at all. I just focus strictly on controlling and limiting the amount of food I eat. That is the only way I manage my weight.
Have you experienced any menstrual irregularities, such as amenorrhea, or other physical symptoms like hair loss, cold intolerance, or fatigue, as a result of your restrictive eating habits?

I've missed my period for a few months and noticed some hair thinning, but honestly, it's not a big deal. It's probably just from stress, and I don't think it has anything to do with my diet. I feel completely fine otherwise.
Don't you think that your restrictive eating habits and significant weight loss might be connected to your missed periods and hair thinning, rather than just stress?

No, I really don't think they are connected at all. I've been under an immense amount of stress with school lately, and that is definitely what is causing those issues. My eating habits are completely fine and have absolutely nothing to do with it.
